title: Local generic-basis subtraction criterion
statement: Let (R,m) be a local ring and R\to S a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings with geometrically integral fibres. Let q\in Spec(S) lie over m, let N be a finite S-module, and let \alpha :S^{\oplus r}\to N be S-linear. Write \xi =mS, which is prime because the fibre S\otimes_R\kappa(m) is a domain. Assume N_q is flat over R and \alpha\otimes_S\kappa(\xi):\kappa(\xi)^{\oplus r}\to N\otimes _S\kappa (\xi ) is an isomorphism. Then \alpha  is universally injective as an R-module map (L\otimes_R\alpha is injective for every R-module L) and (coker \alpha )_q is flat over R. Local rings, spectra, modules, flatness, finite presentation, residue fields, localizations and geometric integrality are [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Because the fibre S/mS is geometrically integral, its underlying ring is a nonzero domain, so ξ=mS is prime. The auxiliary projectivity statement [lem-trf-local-fibres-integral-projective], applied to R→S, makes S projective as an R-module; hence S^{\oplus r} is projective over R. The hypothesis gives that N_q is flat over R.

proof.text: Consider the induced map (S/mS)^{\oplus r}→N_q/mN_q. If an element of the source maps to zero, then after localizing at the generic prime ξ its image is zero; the assumed isomorphism α⊗_Sκ(ξ) therefore makes the element zero in κ(ξ)^{\oplus r}. Since S/mS is a domain, it injects into its fraction field κ(ξ), so the original element was zero. Thus the reduction map is injective. Applying [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] to S^{\oplus r}→N_q over the local ring R gives that this map is universally injective over R.

source.place: Tag 05I3, proof of lemma-induction-step, paragraph beginning “Because S/mS is a domain”; Tag 05FQ.

proof.text: The map S^{\oplus r}→N_q is the composite of α with the localization map N→N_q. For every R-module L, injectivity of L⊗_R(S^{\oplus r})→L⊗_R N_q implies injectivity of L⊗_Rα, because the latter is the first factor of that composite; hence α is universally injective. Localizing at q preserves universal injectivity by [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-localization]. Therefore 0→S_q^{\oplus r}→N_q→(coker α)_q→0 is universally exact. Its middle term is R-flat, so [lem-trf-local-ui-flat-cokernel] gives that (coker α)_q is R-flat.
